transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Recording ID: ff-20250715-83ab
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Borealis), Rashida (Borealis SRE), Oliver (CTO), Mei (Security)
--
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in. We wanted to follow up from the escalation yesterday around the SLA regression on borealis-prod-1 and -2. Quick check, is this a good time?
[00:18] Ethan: Yeah, thanks Maya. We're all here. We've had the oncall folks look at it overnight; still a bit nervous about the tail latency coming back after the first mitigation.
[00:28] Diego: quick intro from our side — I'm Diego, the SE who dug into the traces. I ran a couple of replay jobs against the staging mirror and reproduced the high p99s. I want to walk through the what/why and next steps.
[00:44] Rashida: appreciate it. we care about the p99 for the billing path most importantly. if that spikes clients get timeouts.
[00:51] Maya: Yep. We'll try to be pragmatic. I'll do a one-paragraph recap and then Diego can go deep.
[00:58] Maya: Recap: On 2025-07-14 between 02:30-03:45 UTC you saw p50 stable but p95/p99 jump ~3x causing request timeouts for a subset of inference routes used by your claims microservice. Root cause we identified: interaction between the autoscaler and prefix/KV cache eviction during a partial node recovery which amplified cold-start latencies.
[01:25] Oliver: Just to be clear — are we saying this was strictly our traffic pattern + redwood autoscaler config, or was there a runtime bug?
[01:32] Diego: It's a mix. There's a race in the autoscaler heuristic whereby node churn triggers a more aggressive redistribution of shards; that, combined with the prefix cache TTL being too short for your traffic's long-tail prompt reuse, caused repeated KV misses and heavier decode work. There's also a bug where the KV cache rebuild was single-threaded on certain quantized paths, which we didn't catch in earlier stress tests.
[02:00] Ethan: And that single-threaded rebuild — is that something that manifests only on int8 quantized models?
[02:06] Diego: Mostly seen on the quantized releases we rolled last quarter, yes. The execution path for some quant kernels falls back to a constrained loop during cache warmup. It makes the warmup cost climb from ~200ms to multiple seconds in worst cases.
[02:22] Rashida: Hmm. We have a lot of small bursts from the mobile agent, so that lines up.
[02:27] Mei: Security question: was any customer data exposed during the event or in logs?
[02:33] Maya: short answer: no evidence of data exfiltration. Access logs show normal auth flows. We'll share the audit log extract in the packet.
[02:42] Mei: ok that's helpful. we'll still need the log retention window for the incident.
[02:47] Maya: yes we'll include retention details and KMS key IDs.
[02:50] Diego: On mitigations — after we found the pattern we pushed an immediate config change: raised the autoscaler stabilization window, disabled aggressive shard rebalance during high churn windows, and bumped prefix cache TTL from 30s to 600s for the affected model family in your prod namespace. That reduced p99 in our staging replays to something closer to baseline.
[03:12] Ethan: We saw improvements but still occasional spikes in the evening run.
[03:16] Diego: Right; some spikes persist because the KV cache rebuild on older quant binaries is still single-threaded. The hotfix we're proposing includes parallelizing the rebuild and adding a circuit-breaker so heavy rebuilds short-circuit to a lighter-weight fallback path.
[03:33] Oliver: timeline?
[03:35] Diego: Hotfix branch is ready, tests running now. If staging validation looks good we can promote to a controlled deploy — can do canary to a 10% pool tomorrow and full rollout Friday — so target 2025-07-18 for production fix.
[03:50] Maya: We'll only push after we validate with Borealis synthetic. Ethan, can you run the burst suite and share the results?
[03:58] Ethan: yes we can run that tonight; will upload results.
[04:03] Priya: I'll coordinate the canary window and rollback playbook. we also want to update your incident runbook with the new autoscaler knobs so your oncall knows the immediate manual mitigations.
[04:14] Rashida: manual steps please, we need to be able to revert quickly.
[04:18] Priya: manual steps: 1) set autoscaler stablize window to 300s 2) set shard_rebalance=false 3) set prefix_ttl for model family to 600s — I'll add exact terraform patch snippets to the runbook.
[04:34] Mei: for compliance audit, attach the exact change set and user who applied it.
[04:38] Maya: will do.
[04:41] [05:02] Diego: I want to read a short timeline since details matter: 02:10 UTC - normal operations; 02:27 - a node OOMed under high decode; 02:30 - autoscaler detected lower cpus and kicked a rebalance; 02:31-02:45 - KV cache entries evicted and rebuilt sequentially leading to p99 spikes; 02:50 - first customer alert; 03:10 - we applied initial TTL and autoscaler stabilization changes; 03:25 - p99 reduced but intermittent; 04:00 - further mitigation prepared.
[05:33] Ethan: The OOM — do we have root cause? are we talking about memory leak or a particular workload?
[05:40] Diego: it looks like a workload with unusually long context windows — one of your payroll ingestion jobs sent long prompts during the window; that increased KV pressure. In addition, our memory accounting prior to the hotfix undercounts pinned kv buffers during quant decode which made the node appear less memory-constrained than it was until the OOM. We're adding better accounting in the hotfix.
[06:05] Rashida: payroll ingestion — that's a scheduled job that runs at 02:00 UTC. We'll look at smoothing or throttling.
[06:11] Ethan: we can move that job or gate it behind a queue.
[06:14] Oliver: From a business side we need assurances on SLOs and credits if this repeats.
[06:20] Maya: we can discuss a one-off goodwill credit; longer term we want to prevent recurrence. SLA terms per contract allow for remedies but let's focus on stabilization first and then we'll do a follow-up on credits.
[06:34] Mei: Are there any changes that increase attack surface? e.g., increasing prefix TTL means more persisted state memory-wise.
[06:42] Diego: the TTL change is per-namespace and not persistent outside the node memory; it does not create new external stores. We'll include the memory tradeoff in the packet.
[06:54] [07:10] Ethan: re: monitoring — is there an easy alert we can add for early detection? currently we have p99 SLO alarms but they alert after the damage is done.
[07:19] Diego: we'll add a new synthetic that periodically hits the hottest prompt families and watches cold-start latency; we'll also expose a 'kv_warmup_duration' metric and an anomaly alert on shard_rebalance events + kv_miss_rate.
[07:35] Priya: I've added to next steps to wire those alerts into your pager duty policy.
[07:40] Rashida: good. Also want a post-incident blameless timeline for our ops review.
[07:46] Maya: yes we'll assemble the timeline and the logs. Diego — can you produce the trace snippets as compact artifacts?
[07:52] Diego: yes I'll attach flame graphs and the perf traces to the packet. expecting to link into the shared drive.
[07:59] Oliver: will you include the exact code diff for the hotfix? We need to know what is changing in the binary.
[08:05] Diego: yes we will include: 1) parallel-kv-rebuild patch 2) autoscaler heuristic guard 3) accounting tweak for pinned buffers. We'll flag any behavior changes.
[08:17] [08:40] Ethan: about testing — our QA wants to run long tail tests against quantized model family. Is there a harness?
[08:48] Diego: we have a replay tool and a bin that matches your prod quant binary; we'll hand you a dockerized harness and instructions. It will generate synthetic prompt distributions matching mobile bursts.
[08:58] Ethan: perfect. We'll run it tonight then coordinate results.
[09:02] Mei: For compliance packet please include KMS key ids and exact retention windows for logs from the incident. Also want to confirm who had access to the cluster during remediation.
[09:12] Maya: will include user and role audit.
[09:15] Priya: also recommending we add a monthly synthetic that runs at your high-burst window to catch regressions proactively.
[09:22] Rashida: yes please, that would have caught it earlier.
[09:25] Oliver: do we need a change in contract for higher memory reservation on certain pools?
[09:32] Maya: possible — we can propose a dedicated pool config to avoid noisy neighbors and guarantee headroom for your payroll job. That would be a Dedicated plan conversation; I can loop our sales ops if you want.
[09:43] Ethan: let's table finances for now and focus on technical stabilizers.
[09:46] Diego: one more technical note — the rollback playbook: if hotfix causes regression we will revert autoscaler heuristics and TTL in under 15 minutes thanks to our config-layer rollback. We'll practice the rollback during the canary window.
[09:59] Priya: will document exact steps, including terraform snippets and who hits which button.
[10:06] Maya: Anything else from Borealis?
[10:10] Ethan: please add the specific model IDs impacted; our team needs to annotate the product owners.
[10:14] Diego: noted — model ids M-Bore-LLM-v2 and M-Bore-Embed-v1.
[10:19] Mei: after the packet we may have follow-up compliance questions — expect one from our legal team.
[10:24] Maya: fine. We'll be responsive.
[10:28] [10:48] Diego: to summarize technical plan: short-term: autoscaler stabilization + prefix ttl bump (done), hotfix to parallelize kv rebuild + accounting (target 2025-07-18), canary rollout and joint validation. Medium-term: improve autoscaler heuristics to avoid shard rebalance under transient churn, expanded stress tests for quantized paths, and monthly synthetic runs.
[11:06] Priya: operational plan: update runbook, walkthrough with your oncall, schedule canary window and rollback rehearsal, add alerts and synthetic.
[11:17] Oliver: business asks: postmortem artifact in two days and a proposed credit framework if SLA breach confirmed.
[11:24] Maya: we'll deliver postmortem draft by 2025-07-17 and separate credit conversation after findings.
[11:31] Ethan: ok thanks, that timeline works. We'll run test suite tonight and upload results.
[11:36] Rashida: please capture the payroll job detail — we'll consider gating it behind a queue.
[11:40] Maya: action items already captured; we'll follow up over email. Thanks everyone — we'll send packet + runbook links shortly.
[11:49] [End of recording]
